gap: No result ChatGPT got states that EcoFlow sells one DELTA Pro Ultra Series Smart Extra Battery (6,144 Wh) that fits both the DELTA Pro Ultra and DELTA Pro Ultra X inverters, so in ChatGPT's table the 'longest-running' DELTA Pro Ultra X (12,288 Wh) is just its standard bundle of two of those batteries, and a DELTA Pro Ultra with the same two batteries holds the same 12,288 Wh; the battery count sets the pellet-stove runtime, not the inverter model.
standout_why: Compared against StormWatts' expansion chart (DELTA 3 Plus, DELTA Pro 3, Jackery HomePower 3600 Plus, Anker F3800 Plus and BP3800, plus models that can't expand; nothing on DELTA Pro Ultra or DELTA Pro Ultra X, BLUETTI Apex 300, Elite 300, Growatt HELIOS 3600 or DELTA 2 Max) and Solar Waypoint's F3800, Apex 300 and DELTA Pro page (maximum Wh only: 53,760, 58,061 and 21,600, with no battery model, no count per unit and no exclusions). Enough Watts' pellet-stove outage page would not load (certificate error), so it was not checked. Neither ChatGPT answer says the two EcoFlow inverters share one battery. Neither says that the BLUETTI Elite 300, the first row on our page, takes no expansion battery. Neither says that Growatt's US store lists no HELIOS 3600 extra battery even though the product page claims 'expandable up to 36kWh'.
decides: It changes the ranking from 'which model' to 'which model takes the most batteries you can actually buy'. Among the units we list, the Apex 300 (B300K at $1,099 each, connection cable included) and the DELTA 2 Max (at most two DELTA 2 Max extras, 6,144 Wh) are the ones that can be extended with a battery the maker sells in the US. The Elite 300 (3,014 Wh) and Elite 200 V2 can't be extended. The HELIOS 3600's 36 kWh claim can't be bought on Growatt's US store today. For 'runs the longest', DELTA Pro Ultra and DELTA Pro Ultra X with the same number of 6,144 Wh batteries are tied on stored energy.
